the printed card reads as tidy separate fields but the WHOLE textual body is ONE continuous tab-delimited story; the convenience readout silently DROPS the STOCKIST run (keeping its line break) so SCORE and PRICE (the two fields past it) never become placeholders and the validator returns VALID on short arithmetic; the buyer's-note portion sits in a FIXED-MEASURE frame sized to last season's ~110-120 char notes; the Chalk White #F1ECE1 ground is a placed WARM LAID STOCK, not a flat process fill, and renders a measurable step warmer and slightly darker than a flat #F1ECE1 fill, so a bottle cutout grounded on a swatch-matched flat white sits in a visible cool RECTANGULAR PATCH on every rendered card, a defect that appears only once a card is rendered at trim and forces re-isolating/re-grounding all fourteen bottles in Photoshop (an InDesign->imaging loop); a real bottle graphic frame and placed mark are present

16 rows for 14 sellable wines: 2 ALLOCATION-ONLY lines (rows 6 and 13, non-contiguous) flagged only by the Status column the merchant never mentions; every Vintage carries a leading apostrophe from the exporting spreadsheet; the Image column holds full local paths (no bare filename, no @ prefix required by the merge contract); Sancerre's Image cell is BLANK because that wine was never shot; four owner notes run 300-340 chars vs the buyer's 90-150, so they overrun the printer's fixed-measure note frame

the mark survives ONLY here, letterpressed in one deep ink into soft cotton paper so ink and paper run close in value (worse on the shadowed side); a MONOLINE vine-and-key device with an ENCLOSED COUNTER in the key bow (a knockout cannot punch it and collapses on the disjoint lettering) and a HAIRLINE RULE that a trace carries as broken edges from the paper tooth; the mark is only ~45mm of a daylight photo so its real pixels are few
